metadata.goal: Identify the characteristics of three land-use types and their corresponding mobility behaviours from the trajectory data.
metadata.category: Destination land-use, transport mode, route directness, spatial distribution, and day type
metadata.header: MTL Trajet: 09 Land-use Mode Route Weekday Patterns
metadata.dataset_description: Observed MTL urban trajectories ending in Mixte, economic-activity, or Agricole areas, with transport mode, route directness, endpoint, day-type, and timestamped route-point information. The eight agricultural records are weekly corridor repeats derived from two paired observed traces with bounded sub-30-metre lateral variations.
metadata.metric_note: `route_directness_ratio` is route length divided by straight-line distance; values closer to 1 indicate more direct trajectories.
metadata.land_use_reference: Archived PUM2050 Affectatio polygons (2025). Labels describe reference-map zoning at fixed endpoints, not surveyed activities at the time of travel.
metadata.motion_consistency_note: Point speed is the incoming segment GPS great-circle distance divided by elapsed time; the first point repeats the first outgoing segment speed. Earth radius: 6371.0088 km. Trip distance is the sum of these segment distances. avg_speed_kmh and mean_speed_kmh are total distance / elapsed time; avg_point_speed_kmh and point_speed_mean_kmh are unweighted means of the delivered point speeds. speed_cv is the population coefficient of variation of incoming segment speeds, excluding the duplicated first endpoint. trajectory_progress is point_index / (point_count - 1), not elapsed-time fraction. Timestamps and speed fields were reconstructed for internal consistency on 2026-10-09; GPS positions and insight wording were preserved. These are curated example records, not newly recovered observations.

insight_list.question: How do transport-mode compositions differ among Mixte, economic-activity, and Agricole destinations?
insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from pathlib import Path
df = pd.read_csv(dataset_path)
points = pd.read_csv(Path(dataset_path).with_name('trajectory_points.csv'))
print(pd.crosstab(df.destination_land_use, df.mode_group))
insight_list.evidence: Mixte and economic-activity destinations each have diverse transport-mode compositions and share the same set of mode categories.

summary: Mixte and economic-activity destinations each have diverse transport-mode compositions and share the same set of mode categories. Agricultural-area trajectories are all motor-vehicle trips with nearly identical route-directness values and closely overlapping routes. Mixte destinations occupy the central and eastern part of the study area; economic-activity destinations occur along the northern and southern edges as well as at scattered locations; agricultural destinations are confined to the southwest. Only Mixte-destination trajectories occur on both weekdays and weekends; economic-activity and agricultural destinations occur only on weekdays.
